phrase: my kid lands a skateboard trick and I want it to look like a skate video
interpretation: The look you named is, in film language: fisheye skate video. An extremely wide lens is very low and very close. The ground rushes past. Straight lines bend at the edges of the frame. The light is plain daylight. The camera rides along with the person.
A hit, a catch or a landing is a contact. Show the move wide, then the contact tight, at full speed from the contact.
Air moments read best from a low camera, with a real height and real gravity.
subject: a kid on a skateboard
action: landing a kickflip off a low kerb
setting: an empty car park on a grey day

options.label: A
options.plain: The camera sits on the floor with a wide lens and looks along the ground. The subject towers.
options.movement: locked: the camera does not move, the action comes to it
options.placement: on the floor, 3 m away, the lens level and looking along the ground into the light
options.lens_why: An ultra-wide lens on the floor makes the ground rush to the lens and gives a small jump real scale.

risks: Do not tilt the lens up at the face: it bends bodies and generators stretch them. Keep the lens level.
Slow motion plus a jump invites floating. Write a real height and real gravity.
